 New ‘Hunger Games’ prequel traces trauma behind future rebellion
 By Danielle Broadway via Reuters - November 20, 2026 - 7:00 AM 318 Share Facebook Twitter "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" promotional poster. (Hunger Games via Facebook) SPONSORED ARTICLES

 LOS ANGELES  —   The new “Hunger Games” prequel explores how young Haymitch Abernathy’s ordeal in a deadly televised contest shapes him and helps sow the seeds of the rebellion against his country’s oppressive rulers depicted in the later films.
 The films follow children, called tributes, who are forced to fight to the death in a televised spectacle staged by the rulers of the fictional nation of Panem.
 Joseph Zada, who plays Haymitch in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” opening in US theaters on Friday, said he had to immerse himself in the character’s suffering, with each devastating moment presenting a new emotional challenge.
 “It was such a tough emotional journey to try and have each of those really destroying moments feel different,” Zada said. The film shows how those experiences shaped Haymitch’s alcoholism and abrasive demeanor.
 The sixth film in the franchise based on Suzanne Collins’ dystopian novels turns back the clock to show how Haymitch became the hardened mentor who would later help a new generation challenge Panem’s rulers. Woody Harrelson played the older Haymitch in the earlier films.
 “Sunrise on the Reaping” serves as both a sequel to the film “The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes” and a prequel to the four original “Hunger Games” films starring Jennifer Lawrence.
 Maya Hawke, who plays a young Wiress, a former Hunger Games victor who would later join the rebellion against Panem’s rulers, said the film’s depiction of “human pain” also carried a message about social change.
 “It actually takes a lot of efforts, failed efforts, to make change,” Hawke said.
 The film also stars Mckenna Grace, Whitney Peak and Ben Wang. Grace and Wang said they had grown up with the books, with Wang recalling “the height of ‘Hunger Games’ mania.”
